name: BMP280
full_name: BMP280 Digital Barometric Pressure and Temperature Sensor (GY-BMP280 module)
subcategory: digital barometric pressure and temperature sensor
description: Digital barometric pressure and temperature sensor from Bosch Sensortec, commonly sold on the small GY-BMP280 breakout with an onboard 3.3 V regulator. It measures pressure from 300 to 1100 hPa and temperature from -40 to +85 C, and supports both I2C and SPI. On I2C the SDO pin selects the 7-bit address (0x76 low, 0x77 high). The bare chip is an LGA-8 that is not hand-solderable, so the breakout header is the practical form for hobbyists.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: module supply (board regulator typically accepts 3.3-5 V depending on variant)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (or SPI SCK in 4-wire SPI mode)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (or SPI SDI/MOSI in SPI mode)

pins.name: CSB
pins.description: chip select; high = I2C mode, pull low to select SPI

pins.name: SDO
pins.description: I2C address select (low=0x76, high=0x77); SPI data out (MISO) in SPI mode

extra.interface: I2C (up to 3.4 MHz) and SPI (3- and 4-wire)

typical_application: Altitude estimation, indoor barometric/weather sensing, and drone/altimeter applications via I2C or SPI to an MCU.
gotchas: default I2C address depends on SDO: 0x76 when low (most GY-BMP280 boards default here), 0x77 when high; libraries often assume 0x77 so this is a frequent no-device error
the BMP280 chip operates at 1.71-3.6 V (VDDIO down to 1.2 V); only the GY breakout regulator tolerates 5 V, never put 5 V on the bare chip
BMP280 measures pressure + temperature only - it has NO humidity sensor; the pin-compatible BME280 adds humidity and is easily confused
GY-BMP280 header order varies by board revision (this VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, CSB, SDO order is the common one); always confirm against the silkscreen
pulling CSB low switches the chip to SPI mode; for I2C keep CSB high (boards usually tie it high)
the chip-ID register tells siblings apart: 0x58 for BMP280 vs 0x60 for BME280, since both share the 0x76/0x77 I2C range
